title: Midwestern trees
subtitle: 39 common trees of Midwest forests, yards and riverbanks
description: Learn each tree the way you meet it outside: its overall shape, its bark, its leaf, and its fruit or seed.

cards.name: White oak
cards.subtitle: Quercus alba
cards.summary: The classic oak: rounded lobes with no bristle tips and pale, flaky bark.

cues.overall: Broad, spreading crown with stout, horizontal limbs
cues.bark: Light ash-gray, in loose vertical plates or scales
cues.leaf: Rounded lobes, no bristle tips; turns wine-red in fall
cues.fruit: Oval acorn with a shallow, warty cap; matures in one year

cards.name: Bur oak
cards.subtitle: Quercus macrocarpa
cards.summary: The prairie oak, with a fringed acorn cap and a leaf pinched at the waist.
facts: Prairie fires, thanks to thick bark

cues.overall: Rugged, wide crown with thick, crooked limbs
cues.bark: Thick, dark gray, deeply ridged and corky
cues.leaf: Wide rounded top over a deep pinch near the middle
cues.fruit: Large acorn with a mossy, fringed cap

cards.name: Northern red oak
cards.subtitle: Quercus rubra
cards.summary: Pointed, bristle-tipped lobes and bark with shiny 'ski trail' stripes.

cues.overall: Tall, straight trunk with a rounded crown
cues.bark: Dark ridges with flat, shiny gray stripes running up them
cues.leaf: Lobes cut halfway to the midrib, each with bristle tips
cues.fruit: Barrel-shaped acorn with a flat, beret-like cap

cards.name: Pin oak
cards.subtitle: Quercus palustris
cards.summary: A pyramid-shaped oak whose lower branches droop and keep dead leaves in winter.

cues.overall: Pyramid shape: upper limbs up, middle level, lower limbs drooping
cues.bark: Smooth gray-brown, with shallow ridges as it ages
cues.leaf: Deeply cut, U- or C-shaped gaps, 5-7 bristly lobes
cues.fruit: Small round acorn, often striped, with a thin saucer cap

cards.name: Swamp white oak
cards.subtitle: Quercus bicolor
cards.summary: A bottomland oak with two-toned leaves: dark green above, silvery-white below.

cues.overall: Broad, open crown, often with drooping lower branches
cues.bark: Gray-brown with deep furrows; upper limbs peel in papery scales
cues.leaf: Shallow, wavy lobes; pale fuzzy underside
cues.fruit: Acorns in pairs on a long stalk

cards.name: Sugar maple
cards.subtitle: Acer saccharum
cards.summary: The maple-syrup tree, with blazing orange fall color and a leaf like the Canadian flag.

cues.overall: Dense, oval crown; brilliant orange and yellow in fall
cues.bark: Gray, furrowed into firm, curling plates
cues.leaf: 5 lobes with few large teeth and rounded notches
cues.fruit: U-shaped pair of winged seeds (samaras)

cards.name: Red maple
cards.subtitle: Acer rubrum
cards.summary: Something is red in every season: buds, flowers, leaf stems and fall leaves.
facts: Tiny red flowers in early spring

cues.overall: Oval crown; scarlet early in fall
cues.bark: Smooth and light gray when young, later shaggy plates
cues.leaf: 3 main lobes with saw-toothed edges and V-shaped notches
cues.fruit: Small red winged seeds in spring

cards.name: Silver maple
cards.subtitle: Acer saccharinum
cards.summary: A fast riverbank maple with deeply cut leaves that flash silver underneath in wind.

cues.overall: Wide, vase-like crown; often several trunks
cues.bark: Gray, peeling in long, shaggy strips on older trees
cues.leaf: Deeply cut lobes, almost to the middle; silvery underside
cues.fruit: Large winged seeds that drop in late spring

cards.name: Boxelder
cards.subtitle: Acer negundo
cards.summary: The maple that doesn't look like one: its leaves are split into 3-5 leaflets.

cues.overall: Irregular, often leaning, with several trunks
cues.bark: Light brown, with narrow ridges and shallow furrows
cues.leaf: 3-5 coarsely toothed leaflets, like poison ivy's shape
cues.fruit: V-shaped winged seeds hanging in clusters through winter

cards.name: Shagbark hickory
cards.subtitle: Carya ovata
cards.summary: Unmistakable bark that peels in long strips, like a shaggy coat.

cues.overall: Tall, straight trunk with an oblong crown
cues.bark: Long gray strips curling away at both ends
cues.leaf: 5 leaflets; the top 3 are much larger
cues.fruit: Round nut in a thick husk that splits into 4

cards.name: Bitternut hickory
cards.subtitle: Carya cordiformis
cards.summary: Spot it in winter by its sulfur-yellow buds.

cues.overall: Tall and straight with a narrow, rounded crown
cues.bark: Gray with tight, shallow, interlacing ridges
cues.leaf: 7-11 narrow leaflets; bright yellow buds at the tips
cues.fruit: Small round nut with 4 thin ridges on the husk

cards.name: Black walnut
cards.subtitle: Juglans nigra
cards.summary: Long feathery leaves, dark diamond-patterned bark and green tennis-ball fruit.
facts: Release juglone, which stunts nearby plants

cues.overall: Open, rounded crown; leafs out late, drops leaves early
cues.bark: Dark brown to black, ridges in a diamond pattern
cues.leaf: Long leaf with many pointed leaflets; the end one is often missing
cues.fruit: Round green husk that stains hands brown

cards.name: American basswood
cards.subtitle: Tilia americana
cards.summary: Huge heart-shaped leaves and fragrant summer flowers that bees love.

cues.overall: Tall, dense, oval crown; often sprouts from the base
cues.bark: Gray with narrow, flat-topped ridges
cues.leaf: Big, heart-shaped, toothed, with an uneven base
cues.fruit: Pea-sized nutlets hanging from a leafy wing

cards.name: Eastern cottonwood
cards.subtitle: Populus deltoides
cards.summary: A massive riverbank tree with triangle leaves and cottony seeds in early summer.

cues.overall: Huge, broad crown; massive trunk near water
cues.bark: Thick, gray, with deep furrows
cues.leaf: Triangle-shaped with flat stems, so they flutter
cues.fruit: Strings of capsules releasing cotton-tufted seeds

cards.name: Quaking aspen
cards.subtitle: Populus tremuloides
cards.summary: White-barked groves whose round leaves tremble in the slightest breeze.
facts: In clonal groves from shared roots

cues.overall: Slim trunks in groves; golden yellow in fall
cues.bark: Smooth, pale white-green with black scars
cues.leaf: Nearly round with a short point; trembles on flat stems
cues.fruit: Fuzzy catkins in spring

cards.name: Black willow
cards.subtitle: Salix nigra
cards.summary: A leaning streamside tree with long, narrow leaves.

cues.overall: Often leaning over water with several trunks
cues.bark: Dark brown-black, deep furrows and shaggy ridges
cues.leaf: Lance-shaped, 3-6 in long, finely toothed
cues.fruit: Catkins in spring

cards.name: American sycamore
cards.subtitle: Platanus occidentalis
cards.summary: The ghost of the river bottoms: camouflage bark peeling to bright white limbs.
facts: Among the widest in the East

cues.overall: Massive trunk; white upper limbs stand out in winter
cues.bark: Patchwork of brown, green and cream; white higher up
cues.leaf: Very large with shallow lobes and big teeth
cues.fruit: Round, bristly seed balls hanging all winter

cards.name: Common hackberry
cards.subtitle: Celtis occidentalis
cards.summary: Bark covered in odd corky warts and ridges.

cues.overall: Rounded crown; often a city or fencerow tree
cues.bark: Gray with warty, corky ridges
cues.leaf: Uneven base, long pointed tip, toothed edge
cues.fruit: Small purple berries on long stems

cards.name: American elm
cards.subtitle: Ulmus americana
cards.summary: The vase-shaped street tree of old Main Streets, thinned by Dutch elm disease.

cues.overall: Vase shape: limbs fan up and arch over like a fountain
cues.bark: Gray, ridged; cut a ridge to see layers of brown and white
cues.leaf: Oval, double-toothed, with an uneven base
cues.fruit: Flat, round papery wafers with a notched tip

cards.name: Black cherry
cards.subtitle: Prunus serotina
cards.summary: Bark like burnt potato chips, and shiny leaves that smell of almond when crushed.

cues.overall: Oval crown on a straight trunk
cues.bark: Dark, flaky plates like burnt potato chips
cues.leaf: Shiny, narrow, finely toothed; fuzz along the midrib below
cues.fruit: Hanging clusters of small dark cherries

cards.name: Honey locust
cards.subtitle: Gleditsia triacanthos
cards.summary: Fern-like leaves, long twisting pods and (in the wild) huge branched thorns.
facts: Up to 8 in long, in clusters

cues.overall: Airy, open crown with dappled shade
cues.bark: Dark, with scaly plates; wild trees bear clusters of thorns
cues.leaf: Fine, fern-like leaflets that turn yellow early
cues.fruit: Long, flat, twisting brown pods

cards.name: Black locust
cards.subtitle: Robinia pseudoacacia
cards.summary: Rope-like bark, rounded leaflets and fragrant white flower clusters in May.

cues.overall: Narrow, open crown, often in thickets
cues.bark: Deep, criss-crossing ridges like twisted rope
cues.leaf: Oval leaflets with smooth edges; paired spines at the base
cues.fruit: Short, flat, papery brown pods

cards.name: Kentucky coffeetree
cards.subtitle: Gymnocladus dioicus
cards.summary: Huge doubly compound leaves, thick leathery pods and very few, stout twigs.
facts: Up to 3 ft long, doubly compound
Toxic raw; once roasted as a coffee stand-in

cues.overall: Coarse, stark branches in winter; leafs out late
cues.bark: Gray with thin, scaly ridges curling at the edges
cues.leaf: Enormous leaf of many small oval leaflets
cues.fruit: Thick, leathery, red-brown pods

cards.name: Ohio buckeye
cards.subtitle: Aesculus glabra
cards.summary: Hand-like leaves of five leaflets and the glossy brown 'buckeye' nut.

cues.overall: Rounded crown; one of the first trees to leaf out
cues.bark: Gray, broken into thick scaly plates
cues.leaf: 5 leaflets spread like fingers from one point
cues.fruit: Spiny husk around a shiny brown nut with a pale eye

cards.name: White ash
cards.subtitle: Fraxinus americana
cards.summary: Diamond-patterned bark and paired leaflets; hard hit by the emerald ash borer.

cues.overall: Straight trunk with an oval crown; purple-maroon in fall
cues.bark: Tight diamond-shaped ridges, like a net
cues.leaf: 5-9 leaflets, pale underneath, in opposite pairs
cues.fruit: Single paddle-shaped winged seeds in clusters

cards.name: Tulip tree
cards.subtitle: Liriodendron tulipifera
cards.summary: A towering tree with tulip-shaped leaves and green-orange tulip flowers. Indiana's state tree.

cues.overall: Very tall, ruler-straight trunk, branching high
cues.bark: Gray with tight, interlacing pale furrows
cues.leaf: Four lobes with a squared-off tip, like a tulip or a T-shirt
cues.fruit: Upright cone-like clusters of winged seeds

cards.name: Paper birch
cards.subtitle: Betula papyrifera
cards.summary: Chalk-white bark that peels like paper, in the northern Midwest.

cues.overall: Slim white trunks, often in clumps
cues.bark: Bright white, peeling in thin papery sheets
cues.leaf: Oval with a pointed tip and doubly toothed edge
cues.fruit: Hanging catkins of tiny winged seeds

cards.name: River birch
cards.subtitle: Betula nigra
cards.summary: Salmon-pink bark peeling in curly, papery layers along streams.

cues.overall: Several leaning trunks in a clump
cues.bark: Peeling curls of salmon, tan and cream
cues.leaf: Wedge or diamond shaped with coarse double teeth
cues.fruit: Short upright catkins shedding seeds in early summer

cards.name: American beech
cards.subtitle: Fagus grandifolia
cards.summary: Smooth elephant-gray bark and papery leaves that hang on into winter.
facts: Straight veins, each ending in a tooth

cues.overall: Wide, dense crown; pale tan leaves cling in winter
cues.bark: Smooth, silver-gray, like an elephant's leg
cues.leaf: Neat parallel veins, each ending in a small tooth
cues.fruit: Spiny husk with two triangular nuts

cards.name: American hophornbeam
cards.subtitle: Ostrya virginiana
cards.summary: A small understory tree with very hard wood and hop-like seed clusters. Also called ironwood.
facts: One of the hardest in North America

cues.overall: Small understory tree with a rounded crown
cues.bark: Brown, in thin, shreddy strips curling at the ends
cues.leaf: Oval, pointed, sharply double-toothed
cues.fruit: Papery sacs in clusters, like hops

cards.name: Eastern redbud
cards.subtitle: Cercis canadensis
cards.summary: Pink-purple flowers bursting straight from bare branches in April, then heart leaves.
facts: Before the leaves, in early spring

cues.overall: Small tree, wide and flat-topped; pink cloud in spring
cues.bark: Dark, smooth when young, later scaly; flowers even sprout from the trunk
cues.leaf: Perfect heart shape with a smooth edge
cues.fruit: Flat, pea-like pods

cards.name: Flowering dogwood
cards.subtitle: Cornus florida
cards.summary: White four-petal 'flowers' in spring and alligator-skin bark.
facts: Opposite; veins curve toward the tip

cues.overall: Small, layered, flat-topped understory tree
cues.bark: Broken into small square blocks, like alligator skin
cues.leaf: Oval, smooth edges; veins arc toward the tip
cues.fruit: Clusters of glossy red berries in fall

cards.name: Sassafras
cards.subtitle: Sassafras albidum
cards.summary: Three leaf shapes on one tree: mitten, ghost, and plain oval. Twigs smell like root beer.

cues.overall: Often in colonies; orange, red and purple in fall
cues.bark: Red-brown with deep, flat-topped, corky ridges
cues.leaf: Mitten-, ghost- or oval-shaped leaves on the same tree
cues.fruit: Dark blue berries on bright red stalks

cards.name: Pawpaw
cards.subtitle: Asimina triloba
cards.summary: Big tropical-looking leaves and the largest native fruit in North America.

cues.overall: Small understory tree in patches, with drooping leaves
cues.bark: Thin, smooth, gray-brown with small bumps
cues.leaf: Long, broad toward the tip, hanging down
cues.fruit: Green, potato-shaped fruit in clusters

cards.name: Osage orange
cards.subtitle: Maclura pomifera
cards.summary: Bright green, brain-like 'hedge apples' and orange, shredding bark.
facts: As living fences, before barbed wire

cues.overall: Short trunk with a dense, tangled crown; along fencerows
cues.bark: Orange-brown, in stringy, braided ridges
cues.leaf: Shiny, oval with a long point; thorns on the twigs
cues.fruit: Lumpy yellow-green ball the size of a grapefruit

cards.name: Eastern white pine
cards.subtitle: Pinus strobus
cards.summary: Soft needles in bundles of five (one per letter of W-H-I-T-E).
facts: Tallest trees of the old northern woods

cues.overall: Tall, with layered, horizontal, plume-like branches
cues.bark: Smooth gray-green when young, later dark with deep furrows
cues.leaf: Soft blue-green needles in bundles of five
cues.fruit: Long, slender cones, often sticky with resin

cards.name: Eastern hemlock
cards.subtitle: Tsuga canadensis
cards.summary: Short flat needles with two white stripes below, and a drooping top.

cues.overall: Graceful, with a drooping leader and sweeping branches
cues.bark: Red-brown to gray with deep, scaly ridges
cues.leaf: Short flat needles in two rows, white-striped underneath
cues.fruit: Tiny cones, under an inch, at the branch tips

cards.name: Tamarack
cards.subtitle: Larix laricina
cards.summary: A conifer that turns gold and drops its needles every fall. Lives in northern bogs.
facts: Soft, in tufts of 10-20, shed in fall

cues.overall: Narrow, open cone shape; golden in October
cues.bark: Thin, red-brown and flaky
cues.leaf: Soft needles in tufts on short spurs
cues.fruit: Small, upright, rose-like cones

cards.name: Eastern red cedar
cards.subtitle: Juniperus virginiana
cards.summary: A dense, dark green column on old fields, with shreddy bark and blue berries.

cues.overall: Dense, narrow column or pyramid in old fields
cues.bark: Thin, red-brown, peeling in long fibrous strips
cues.leaf: Tiny overlapping scales; prickly needles on young growth
cues.fruit: Waxy, dusty-blue berry-like cones
